item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I'm… very confused about how the hub defines the ethnic groups. Yeah, I know dreams and dream logic are meant to be confusing, but I'm under the impression that the ethnic groups are supposed to mean something. So, after binging Oneiroi articles from other branches, I think I found some possible answers to my questions. (Also three people apparently downvoted the page since my initial post)

Corporeal (a human)

Alright I can make sense of this one, though can't other corporeal beings also have their own Shadow? This might just boil down to "whatever floats your boat" it seems. I like to consider this canon, though.

Noncon (a dream element)

Free Consciousness (a OneIroi)

What's the difference between these two? Is an Oneiroi that has abandoned its corporeal form a noncorporeal or a free consciousness? Also, does the capitalized "I" mean anything or is it just normal Oneiroi weirdness? It appears I was a big dum-dum, cause for some reason I thought "Noncon" was short for "Non-corporeal." So to answer my question: a Free Consciousness is an Oneiroi that has abandoned its corporeal form. Though I do wonder what the hub page means by:

Free Consciousness (Temporal)

A Noncon, however, is an entity that was dreamt up, having never existed in the real world. For instance, the dreamscape in #Aeliana is dominated by zebra sharks and a centipede whale, which are classifed as Noncons.

Transitory (any kind of visitor)

What sort being can be considered a transitory since it doesn't fall under the other categories? I'm really curious about this one. So, maybe this is supposed to read as "any wandering Oneiroi that don't have a Collective to call home," but I initially read it as "a Transitory is not a Noncon, Free Consciousness, or Corporeal Oneiroi." Which is… a lot more interesting in my opinion, but the only example of this type of thing I can think of (that isn't cringey) is the aspect of an aspect of an Archon.

item.content:encoded:
In the 1930s. There's a clear decade of time between the conflict and the construction of the line and it seemed faintly out of place to me. All the others seem to have a connection to the immediate time of the war, either being a participant country, person or the name of a battle or thing from that time.

By contrast the Maginot line didn't exist at all during that war, and while it was constructed to be the ultimate defense against the kind of war that prevailed during the first world war, it was only ever actually tested during the opening of the second world war, which makes me notionally connect it to that war rather than the first.

Either way it's not important enough to make a bigger deal out of than I already have. It was just something that bugged me.
